File: D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/README.md
--- a/D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/README.md
+++ b/D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/README.md
@@ -1,547 +1,72 @@
-# Magic: The Gathering Card Collection Manager
+# Maps Application
 
-<p align="center">
- <img src="https://via.placeholder.com/200x200/1E88E5/FFFFFF?text=MTG" alt="MTG Collection Manager Logo" width="200"/>
-</p>
+## Overview
 
-A modern Android application for Magic: The Gathering players to manage their card collection, search for cards, track collection value, and organize cards by set or color.
+This Android application focuses on displaying and managing locations on Google Maps. Users can
+view, add, and interact with map markers representing different locations.
 
----
+## Features
 
-## Purpose
+- Google Maps integration
+- View saved locations on the map
+- Add new locations with title and description
+- Get current user location
+- Clean architecture design pattern
 
-This application was created to **make life easier for Magic: The Gathering players** by providing:
-- A centralized place to track your card collection
-- Easy card search powered by the Scryfall API
-- Automatic price tracking and collection value calculation
-- Organization by color, set, or custom filters
-- Persistent storage - your collection is saved across sessions
+## Project Structure
 
-Whether you're a casual player or a serious collector, this app helps you know what cards you own, their value, and what's missing from your collection.
+The project follows a clean architecture approach with the following components:
 
----
+### Presentation Layer
 
-## Features
+- **MapFragment**: UI component for displaying and interacting with the map
+- **MapViewModel**: Handles UI logic and communication with domain layer
+- **Layouts**: Includes map fragment layout and add location dialog
 
-### ✅ Authentication & Session Management
-- Secure email/password registration and login via Firebase
-- Automatic session persistence - no need to log in every time
-- User-specific collections tied to your account
+### Domain Layer
 
-### Card Search
-- Search for any MTG card by name
-- Real-time results from the Scryfall database
-- View card details including:
- - Card image
- - Mana cost, type, and rarity
- - Set information
- - Current market price
+- **Location model**: Data class representing a location with id, title, description, latitude, and
+ longitude
+- **LocationRepository interface**: Defines data operations for locations
+- **Use Cases**:
+ - GetLocationByIdUseCase: Retrieve a specific location
+ - GetLocationsUseCase: Retrieve all saved locations
+ - GetUserLocationUseCase: Get the user's current location
+ - SaveLocationUseCase: Save a new location
 
-### Collection Management
-- Add cards to your collection with:
- - Quantity tracking (how many copies you own)
- - Condition (Near Mint, Lightly Played, etc.)
- - Personal notes
-- View your collection in multiple ways:
- - All cards (chronological)
- - By color (White, Blue, Black, Red, Green, Colorless)
- - By set
-- See individual and total collection value
+### Data Layer
 
-### Value Tracking
-- Automatic price updates from Scryfall
-- Per-card and total collection value
-- Condition-based organization
+- **LocationRepositoryImpl**: Implementation of the location repository
 
-### Modern UI
-- Material Design 3 components
-- Clean, intuitive interface
-- Dark mode support (system default)
-- Smooth animations and transitions
-
----
-
-## How to Use
-
-### Initial Setup
-1. Download and install the app
-2. Launch the app - you'll see a splash screen
-3. Register with your email and password
-4. You're ready to start building your collection!
-
-### Searching for Cards
-1. From the Collection screen, tap the **Search FAB** (floating action button)
-2. Enter a card name in the search bar (e.g., "Lightning Bolt")
-3. Tap **Search** or press Enter
-4. Browse the search results
-5. Tap any card to view details
-
-### Adding Cards to Your Collection
-1. After searching, tap a card to view its details
-2. Set the **Quantity** (number of copies you own)
-3. Select the **Condition** from the dropdown:
- - Near Mint (default)
- - Lightly Played
- - Moderately Played
- - Heavily Played
- - Damaged
-4. Add optional **Notes** (e.g., "Foil", "Signed", etc.)
-5. Tap **Add to Collection**
-6. You'll see a confirmation message
-
-### Viewing Your Collection
-1. The main screen shows your collection
-2. Use the filter buttons at the top:
- - **All Cards**: See everything in chronological order
- - **By Color**: Filter by card color
- - **By Set**: Filter by expansion set
-3. Each card shows:
- - Card image
- - Name and set
- - Quantity you own
- - Condition
- - Total value (price × quantity)
-
-### Statistics (Future Feature)
-- View collection statistics
-- Most valuable cards
-- Breakdown by rarity and color
-
-### Logging Out
-1. Tap the menu icon (three dots) in the Collection screen
-2. Select **Logout**
-3. You'll return to the login screen
-
----
-
-## ️ Technical Architecture
-
-This app follows **industry-standard Android development practices** with a focus on maintainability, testability, and scalability.
-
-### Clean Architecture
-
-The app is structured in three layers with clear separation of concerns:
-
-```
-┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
-│ Presentation Layer (UI) │
-│ - Fragments, ViewModels, Adapters │
-│ - Material Design 3 Components │
-└──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
- │ (UiModels)
-┌──────────────▼──────────────────────────┐
-│ Domain Layer (Business Logic) │
-│ - Use Cases, Models, Repository Ifaces │
-│ - Pure Kotlin (No Android deps) │
-└──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
- │ (Domain Models)
-┌──────────────▼──────────────────────────┐
-│ Data Layer (Data Sources) │
-│ - Repositories, API, Database, DTOs │
-│ - Scryfall API + Room Database │
-└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
-```
-
-**Benefits:**
-- **Testability**: Each layer can be tested independently
-- **Maintainability**: Changes in one layer don't affect others
-- **Scalability**: Easy to add new features or data sources
-
-### SOLID Principles
-
-- **Single Responsibility**: Each class has one reason to change
-- **Open/Closed**: Open for extension, closed for modification
-- **Liskov Substitution**: Interfaces define contracts
-- **Interface Segregation**: Use cases are specific and focused
-- **Dependency Inversion**: Depend on abstractions (repository interfaces)
-
-### MVI (Model-View-Intent) Pattern
-
-Each screen follows the MVI pattern:
-
-```kotlin
-State → User Event → ViewModel → Updated State → UI Update
-```
-
-**Example: Login Screen**
-```kotlin
-// State
-data class State(
- val isLoading: Boolean = false,
- val email: String = "",
- val password: String = ""
-)
-
-// Events (User Actions)
-sealed interface Event {
- data class EmailChanged(val email: String) : Event
- data class PasswordChanged(val password: String) : Event
- data object LoginClicked : Event
-}
-
-// Side Effects (One-time events)
-sealed interface SideEffect {
- data object NavigateToCollection : SideEffect
- data class ShowError(val message: UiText) : SideEffect
-}
-```
-
-**Benefits:**
-- Unidirectional data flow
-- Predictable state management
-- Easy to test and debug
-- Clear separation of UI logic and business logic

-## Design Principles
-
-### No Hardcoded Strings
-All user-facing text is in `res/values/strings.xml`:
-```xml
-<string name="app_name">MTG Collection Manager</string>
-<string name="search_cards">Search for cards…</string>
-```
-
-ViewModels use `UiText` sealed class:
-```kotlin
-sealed class UiText {
- data class DynamicString(val value: String) : UiText()
- class StringResource(@StringRes val resId: Int, vararg val args: Any) : UiText()
-}
-```
-
-### Single ConstraintLayout Root
-All layouts use **ONLY** ConstraintLayout as the root element - no nested layouts:
-```xml
-<androidx.constraintlayout.widget.ConstraintLayout>
- <!-- All views are direct children -->
- <TextView ... />
- <Button ... />
- <RecyclerView ... />
-</androidx.constraintlayout.widget.ConstraintLayout>
-```
-
-**Benefits:**
-- Flat view hierarchy (better performance)
-- Flexible positioning with constraints
-- No unnecessary layout passes
-
-### Kotlin Scope Functions
-Code uses scope functions to avoid repetition:
-```kotlin
-// Bad
-val user = getCurrentUser()
-user.name = "John"
-user.email = "john@example.com"
-return user
-
-// Good
-getCurrentUser().apply {
- name = "John"
- email = "john@example.com"
-}
-```
-
-### Extension Functions
-Common operations are extracted to extensions:
-```kotlin
-// View extensions
-fun View.show() { visibility = View.VISIBLE }
-fun View.hide() { visibility = View.GONE }
-
-// Snackbar extensions
-fun View.showSuccessSnackbar(message: String)
-
-// Image loading extensions
-fun ImageView.loadImage(url: String, isCircle: Boolean = false)
-```

-## Troubleshooting
-
-### Build Errors
-
-**"File google-services.json is missing"**
-- Solution: Follow [FIREBASE_SETUP.md](FIREBASE_SETUP.md) to add the file
-
-**"Unresolved reference: R"**
-- Solution: Clean and rebuild: `Build > Clean Project` then `Build > Rebuild Project`
-
-**"AAPT: error: resource string/app_name not found"**
-- Solution: Ensure `res/values/strings.xml` exists with all required strings
-
-### Runtime Errors
-
-**"FirebaseException: An internal error has occurred"**
-- Solution: Enable Email/Password authentication in Firebase Console
-
-**"Network error"**
-- Solution: Check internet connection and ensure Scryfall API is accessible
-
-**"No cards found"**
-- Solution: Try different search terms (e.g., "Lightning Bolt", "Black Lotus")

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.local
+
+import androidx.room.Entity
+import androidx.room.PrimaryKey
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.domain.model.Location
+
+@Entity(tableName = "locations")
+data class LocationEntity(
+ @PrimaryKey
+ val id: String,
+ val name: String,
+ val latitude: Double,
+ val longitude: Double,
+ val description: String?
+) {
+ // Convert entity to domain model
+ fun toLocation(): Location {
+ return Location(
+ id = id,
+ name = name,
+ latitude = latitude,
+ longitude = longitude,
+ description = description
+ )
+ }
+
+ companion object {
+ // Convert domain model to entity
+ fun fromLocation(location: Location): LocationEntity {
+ return LocationEntity(
+ id = location.id,
+ name = location.name,
+ latitude = location.latitude,
+ longitude = location.longitude,
+ description = location.description
+ )
+ }
+ }
+}

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.local
+
+import androidx.room.Dao
+import androidx.room.Delete
+import androidx.room.Insert
+import androidx.room.OnConflictStrategy
+import androidx.room.Query
+import androidx.room.Update
+import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
+
+@Dao
+interface LocationDao {
+ @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE)
+ suspend fun insertLocation(location: LocationEntity): Long
+
+ @Query("SELECT * FROM locations ORDER BY name ASC")
+ fun getAllLocations(): Flow<List<LocationEntity>>
+
+ @Query("SELECT * FROM locations WHERE id = :id")
+ suspend fun getLocationById(id: String): LocationEntity?
+
+ @Update
+ suspend fun updateLocation(location: LocationEntity)
+
+ @Delete
+ suspend fun deleteLocation(location: LocationEntity)
+
+ @Query("DELETE FROM locations")
+ suspend fun deleteAllLocations()
+}

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.map
+
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.domain.model.Location
+import com.google.android.gms.maps.model.LatLng
+import com.google.maps.android.clustering.ClusterItem
+
+/**
+ * ClusterItem implementation for Location objects
+ */
+class LocationClusterItem(private val location: Location) : ClusterItem {
+
+ override fun getPosition(): LatLng {
+ return LatLng(location.latitude, location.longitude)
+ }
+
+ override fun getTitle(): String? {
+ return location.name
+ }
+
+ override fun getSnippet(): String? {
+ return location.description
+ }
+
+ fun getLocationId(): String {
+ return location.id
+ }
+
+ fun getLocation(): Location {
+ return location
+ }
+}

 31|class MapFragment : Fragment(), OnMapReadyCallback {
 32|
 33| private val viewModel: MapViewModel by viewModels()

 36|
 37| private val requestPermissionLauncher = registerForActivityResult(
 38| ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()
 39| ) { isGranted: Boolean ->
 40| if (isGranted) {
 41| enableMyLocation()
 42| viewModel.getCurrentUserLocation()
 43| } else {
 44| Toast.makeText(
 45| requireContext(),
 46| getString(R.string.location_permission_denied),
 47| Toast.LENGTH_LONG
 48| ).show()
 49| }
 50| }

 53| inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?,
 54| savedInstanceState: Bundle?
 55| ): View? {
 56| return inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_map, container, false)
 57| }

 59| override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
 60| super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
 61| val mapFragment = childFragmentManager.findFragmentById(R.id.map) as SupportMapFragment
 62| mapFragment.getMapAsync(this)
 63|
 64| setupObservers()
 65| setupAddLocationButton(view)
 66| }

 68| private fun setupAddLocationButton(view: View) {
 69| view.findViewById<FloatingActionButton>(R.id.fabAddLocation).setOnClickListener {
 70| userCurrentLocation?.let { location ->
 71| showAddLocationDialog(LatLng(location.latitude, location.longitude))
 72| } ?: run {
 73| Toast.makeText(
 74| requireContext(),
 75| getString(R.string.location_not_available),
 76| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
 77| ).show()
 78| }
 79| }
 80| }

 82| private fun setupObservers() {
 83| viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch {
 84| viewModel.locationsState.collectLatest { state ->
 85| when (state) {
 86| is MapViewModel.LocationsState.Success -> {
 87| displayLocations(state.locations)
 88| }
 89|
 90| is MapViewModel.LocationsState.Error -> {
 91| Toast.makeText(requireContext(), state.message, Toast.LENGTH_LONG).show()
 92| }
 93|
 94| MapViewModel.LocationsState.Loading -> {
 95| // Show loading indicator if needed
 96| }
 97| }
 98| }
 99| }
100|
101| viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch {
102| viewModel.userLocation.collectLatest { state ->
103| when (state) {
104| is MapViewModel.UserLocationState.Success -> {
105| userCurrentLocation = state.location
106| val latLng = LatLng(state.location.latitude, state.location.longitude)
107| googleMap?.moveCamera(CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom(latLng, 15f))
108| }
109|
110| is MapViewModel.UserLocationState.Error -> {
111| Toast.makeText(requireContext(), state.message, Toast.LENGTH_LONG).show()
112| }
113|
114| MapViewModel.UserLocationState.Loading -> {
115| // Show loading indicator if needed
116| }
117| }
118| }
119| }
120| }

122| override fun onMapReady(map: GoogleMap) {
123| googleMap = map
124| checkLocationPermission()
125| googleMap?.setOnMapLongClickListener { latLng ->
126| showAddLocationDialog(latLng)
127| }
128| }

130| private fun checkLocationPermission() {
131| when {
132| ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
133| requireContext(),
134| Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
135| ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED -> {
136| enableMyLocation()
137| }
138|
139| shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) -> {
140| showPermissionRationaleDialog()
141| }
142|
143| else -> {
144| requestPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
145| }
146| }
147| }
148|
149| private fun showPermissionRationaleDialog() {
150| MaterialAlertDialogBuilder(requireContext())
151| .setTitle(R.string.location_permission_title)
152| .setMessage(R.string.location_permission_rationale)
153| .setPositiveButton(R.string.ok) { _, _ ->
154| requestPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
155| }
156| .setNegativeButton(R.string.cancel, null)
157| .show()
158| }
159|
160| private fun enableMyLocation() {
161| try {
162| if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
163| requireContext(),
164| Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
165| ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
166| ) {
167| googleMap?.isMyLocationEnabled = true
168| }
169| } catch (e: SecurityException) {
170| Toast.makeText(
171| requireContext(),
172| getString(R.string.location_permission_denied),
173| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
174| ).show()
175| }
176| }
177|
178| private fun displayLocations(locations: List<Location>) {
179| googleMap?.clear()
180| locations.forEach { location ->
181| val position = LatLng(location.latitude, location.longitude)
182| googleMap?.addMarker(
183| MarkerOptions()
184| .position(position)
185| .title(location.name)
186| .snippet(location.description)
187| )
188| }
189| }

191| private fun showAddLocationDialog(latLng: LatLng) {
192| val dialogView = layoutInflater.inflate(R.layout.dialog_add_location, null)
193| val nameEditText = dialogView.findViewById<com.google.android.material.textfield.TextInputEditText>(
194| R.id.etLocationName
195| )
196| val descriptionEditText =
197| dialogView.findViewById<com.google.android.material.textfield.TextInputEditText>(R.id.etLocationDescription)
198|
199| MaterialAlertDialogBuilder(requireContext())
200| .setTitle(R.string.add_location)
201| .setView(dialogView)
202| .setPositiveButton(R.string.save) { _, _ ->
203| val name = nameEditText.text.toString()
204| val description = descriptionEditText.text.toString()
205|
206| if (name.isNotBlank()) {
207| val newLocation = Location(
208| id = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
209| name = name,
210| description = description,
211| latitude = latLng.latitude,
212| longitude = latLng.longitude
213| )
214| viewModel.saveLocation(newLocation)
215| } else {
216| Toast.makeText(
217| requireContext(),
218| getString(R.string.name_required),
219| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
220| ).show()
221| }
222| }
223| .setNegativeButton(R.string.cancel, null)
224| .show()

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.mapper
+
+import android.location.Location as AndroidLocation
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.domain.model.UserLocation
+
+/**
+ * Mapper extension functions to convert between Android's Location and domain UserLocation
+ */
+fun AndroidLocation?.toUserLocation(): UserLocation? {
+ if (this == null) return null
+ return UserLocation(
+ latitude = this.latitude,
+ longitude = this.longitude,
+ altitude = if (this.hasAltitude()) this.altitude else null,
+ accuracy = if (this.hasAccuracy()) this.accuracy else null,
+ speed = if (this.hasSpeed()) this.speed else null,
+ bearing = if (this.hasBearing()) this.bearing else null,
+ provider = this.provider,
+ time = this.time
+ )
+}

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.domain.common
+
+/**
+ * Represents all possible domain-level errors
+ */
+sealed class DomainError {
+ /**
+ * Error when location services are disabled or unavailable
+ */
+ data object LocationServicesUnavailable : DomainError()
+
+ /**
+ * Error when location permissions are not granted
+ */
+ data object LocationPermissionDenied : DomainError()
+
+ /**
+ * Error when database operations fail
+ */
+ data object DatabaseError : DomainError()
+
+ /**
+ * Error when a requested item is not found
+ */
+ data object ItemNotFound : DomainError()
+
+ /**
+ * General network error
+ */
+ data object NetworkError : DomainError()
+
+ /**
+ * General error with a message
+ */
+ data class GeneralError(val message: String) : DomainError()
+
+ /**
+ * Unknown error when the cause cannot be determined
+ */
+ data class UnknownError(val message: String = "Unknown error occurred") : DomainError()
+}

+++ b/D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/data/common/SafeOperationCall.kt

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.common
+
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.domain.common.DomainError
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.domain.common.Resource
+import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
+import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
+import java.io.IOException
+
+/**
+ * Safely executes a database operation and handles common exceptions
+ */
+suspend fun <T> safeDatabaseCall(dbCall: suspend () -> T): Resource<T> {
+ return try {
+ withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
+ Resource.Success(dbCall())
+ }
+ } catch (throwable: Throwable) {
+ Resource.Error(DomainError.DatabaseError)
+ }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Safely executes a location service call and handles common exceptions
+ */
+suspend fun <T> safeLocationServiceCall(locationCall: suspend () -> T): Resource<T> {
+ return try {
+ withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
+ Resource.Success(locationCall())
+ }
+ } catch (throwable: Throwable) {
+ when (throwable) {
+ is SecurityException -> Resource.Error(DomainError.LocationPermissionDenied)
+ is IOException -> Resource.Error(DomainError.NetworkError)
+ else -> Resource.Error(DomainError.LocationServicesUnavailable)
+ }
+ }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Safely executes any operation and handles common exceptions
+ */
+suspend fun <T> safeCall(call: suspend () -> T): Resource<T> {
+ return try {
+ withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
+ Resource.Success(call())
+ }
+ } catch (throwable: Throwable) {
+ Resource.Error(DomainError.GeneralError(throwable.message ?: "Unknown error"))
+ }
+}

+
+/**
+ * Base fragment that handles ViewBinding
+ */
+abstract class ViewBindingFragment<T : ViewBinding> : BaseFragment() {
+
+ private var _binding: T? = null
+ protected val binding get() = _binding!!
+
+ abstract fun getViewBinding(inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?): T
+
+ override fun onCreateView(
+ inflater: LayoutInflater,
+ container: ViewGroup?,
+ savedInstanceState: Bundle?
+ ): View? {
+ _binding = getViewBinding(inflater, container)
+ return binding.root
+ }
+
+ override fun onDestroyView() {
+ super.onDestroyView()
+ _binding = null
+ }
+}

### String Handling
□ Data layer contains only technical strings (endpoints, DB names, keys)?

### ViewModels
□ All ViewModels extend BaseViewModel?

□ No hardcoded strings in ViewModels?
□ ViewModels use viewModelScope for coroutines?

### Fragments

□ Navigation handled via Navigation Component?
□ No manual Fragment transactions?

### Layouts
□ All layouts have ConstraintLayout as root?
□ No nested ViewGroups (LinearLayout, FrameLayout, RelativeLayout inside)?

□ Dimensions use @dimen references?
□ Strings use @string references?

□ ViewBinding used (no findViewById)?
□ No GlobalScope usage?

### Dependencies

172| true

175| clusterManager?.setOnClusterItemClickListener { item ->

 2|
 3|## Prerequisites
 4|You need a Google account to use Firebase.
 5|
 6|## Steps to Set Up Firebase
 7|
 8|### 1. Create a Firebase Project
 9|
 10|1. Go to [Firebase Console](https://console.firebase.google.com/)
 11|2. Click "Add project" or "Create a project"
 12|3. Enter project name: `MTG Collection Manager` (or any name you prefer)
 13|4. Accept terms and click "Continue"
 14|5. Disable Google Analytics (optional, not needed for this app)
 15|6. Click "Create project"
 16|7. Wait for the project to be created
 17|
 18|### 2. Add Android App to Firebase Project
 19|
 20|1. In your Firebase project dashboard, click the Android icon (or "Add app")
 21|2. Enter the package name: **`com.example.mtgcollectionmanager`** (MUST match exactly)
 22|3. App nickname (optional): `MTG Collection Manager`
 23|4. Debug signing certificate SHA-1 (optional): Leave blank for now
 24|5. Click "Register app"
 25|
 26|### 3. Download google-services.json
 27|
 28|1. After registering, Firebase will prompt you to download `google-services.json`
 29|2. Click "Download google-services.json"
 30|3. **IMPORTANT**: Place this file in the following location:
 31| ```
 32| D:\AndroidProjects\SabaBukia_TBC\app\google-services.json
 33| ```
 34| (The file must be in the `app` directory, NOT in the root project directory)
 35|
 36|4. Click "Next" and then "Continue to console"
 37|
 38|### 4. Enable Firebase Authentication
 39|
 40|1. In Firebase Console, click "Authentication" in the left sidebar
 41|2. Click "Get started"
 42|3. Go to the "Sign-in method" tab
 43|4. Click on "Email/Password"
 44|5. Enable the toggle switch
 45|6. Click "Save"
 46|
 47|
 48|
 49|**Key Points:**
 50|- The `package_name` must be **exactly** `com.example.mtgcollectionmanager`
 51|- The file must be named **exactly** `google-services.json`
 52|- The file must be placed in the **`app/`** directory
 53|
 54|### 6. Sync and Build
 55|
 56|1. After placing the file, open Android Studio
 57|2. Click "Sync Project with Gradle Files"
 58|3. Build the project: `Build > Rebuild Project`
 59|
 60|### Troubleshooting
 61|
 62|**Error: "File google-services.json is missing"**
 63|- Make sure the file is in `app/google-services.json`, not in the project root
 64|
 65|**Error: "Package name doesn't match"**
 66|- Verify the package name in Firebase Console is `com.example.mtgcollectionmanager`
 67|- Re-download the `google-services.json` file
 68|
 69|**Error: "Authentication failed"**
 70|- Make sure Email/Password authentication is enabled in Firebase Console
 71|- Check that you have an internet connection
 72|
 73|**Error: "Plugin [id: 'com.google.gms.google-services'] was not found"**
 74|- This should not happen as the plugin is already configured in `build.gradle.kts`
 75|- If it does, sync Gradle files again
 76|
 77|### Optional: Add Test Users
 78|
 79|To test the app before registering:
 80|1. Go to Firebase Console > Authentication > Users
 81|2. Click "Add user"
 82|3. Enter email and password
 83|4. Click "Add user"
 84|5. Use these credentials in the app
 85|
 86|---
 87|
 88|## Security Notes
 89|
 90|- **NEVER** commit `google-services.json` to a public Git repository
 91|- The file contains API keys but they are safe for client-side use with Firebase security rules
 92|- For production apps, implement Firebase security rules in the Firebase Console
 93|
 94|---
 95|
 96|## Quick Start (After Setup)
 97|
 98|1. Place `google-services.json` in `app/` directory
 99|2. Sync Gradle
100|3. Run the app
101|4. Register a new account or use test credentials
102|5. Start building your MTG card collection!

275|## Technical Details
276|
277|### Database Schema
278|```sql
279|-- Collections Table
280|CREATE TABLE collections (
281| id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
282| name TEXT NOT NULL,
283| description TEXT,
284| createdDate INTEGER NOT NULL,
285| userId TEXT NOT NULL
286|);
287|
288|-- Categories Table
289|CREATE TABLE categories (
290| id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
291| collectionId INTEGER NOT NULL,
292| name TEXT NOT NULL,
293| color TEXT NOT NULL,
294| createdDate INTEGER NOT NULL,
295| FOREIGN KEY(collectionId) REFERENCES collections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
296|);
297|
298|-- Collection Cards Table
299|CREATE TABLE collection_cards (
300| id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
301| collectionId INTEGER NOT NULL,
302| categoryId INTEGER,
303| cardId TEXT NOT NULL,
304| name TEXT NOT NULL,
305| -- ... other fields ...
306| FOREIGN KEY(collectionId) REFERENCES collections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
307| FOREIGN KEY(categoryId) REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
308|);
309|```
310|
311|### MVI Architecture
312|All new screens follow the Model-View-Intent pattern:
313|- **State:** Immutable data class representing UI state
314|- **Event:** Sealed interface for user actions
315|- **SideEffect:** One-time events (navigation, toasts, dialogs)
316|- **ViewModel:** State machine managing business logic
317|
318|### Dependency Injection
319|All components use Hilt:
320|- DAOs provided by `DatabaseModule`
321|- Repositories bound in `CollectionModule`
322|- Use cases auto-injected via constructor
323|- ViewModels annotated with `@HiltViewModel`
324|

341| - Production app would need proper migration strategy

346| - Consider caching collection metadata

351|
352|1. **Database Queries**
353| - All collection queries filtered by userId (security)
354| - Indices on collectionId and categoryId for fast lookups
355| - Flow-based reactive queries prevent stale data

358| - DiffUtil in adapters prevents unnecessary redraws
359| - Coil for efficient image loading and caching
360| - ViewBinding for efficient view access

362|3. **Navigation**

364| - Single activity architecture reduces memory overhead

401|## Design Patterns Used
402|
403|- **MVI (Model-View-Intent):** Clean state management
404|- **Repository Pattern:** Data access abstraction

13| return try {
14| withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
15| Resource.Success(dbCall())
16| }

24| */
25|suspend fun <T> safeLocationServiceCall(locationCall: suspend () -> T): Resource<T> {
26| return try {
27| withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
28| Resource.Success(locationCall())
29| }
30| } catch (throwable: Throwable) {
31| when (throwable) {
32| is SecurityException -> Resource.Error(DomainError.LocationPermissionDenied)
33| is IOException -> Resource.Error(DomainError.NetworkError)
34| else -> Resource.Error(DomainError.LocationServicesUnavailable)
35| }
36| }

All violations have been resolved while maintaining Clean Architecture principles and type safety throughout the codebase!"}]}],"draft_message":"## Project: Location Map Application

### Stack
Kotlin, Coroutines/Flow, Hilt, ViewBinding, Navigation Component, Retrofit, Google Maps SDK

### Architecture
Clean Architecture (data → domain ← presentation). Domain layer: Pure Kotlin, ZERO dependencies. Each layer has own models + mappers (toDomain(), toPresentation()). Resource wrapper, SafeApiCall, handleResponse pattern. UseCases: single-responsibility, all business logic.

### State Management
StateFlow for UI state (single sealed class per screen). SharedFlow for one-time events. UI text: sealed class events with @StringRes Int, resolve in Fragment only.

### Core Requirements

1. Location Permission Flow: Check location permission on app start. If disabled → show permission request dialog. If denied → block app usage, show explanation. Use Permission handling utility/extension.

2. Map Screen: Google Maps integration. Auto-detect device location on launch. Auto-zoom to current location. Zoom in/out buttons on map.

3. Data Loading: Endpoint: https://mocki.io/v1/d7c6d734-6080-4045-a196-7da16339b6d7. Show loader while fetching. Handle error states.

4. Markers: Place markers from API response. Clustering: zoomed out → grouped with count. Unclustered: zoomed in → individual markers. Use Maps Cluster Manager.

5. Marker Click → BottomSheet: Show BottomSheet on marker tap. Display JSON parameters. Height: wrap content (minimal). ConstraintLayout inside, no nesting.

6. Show All Locations Button: Button to fit all markers in viewport. Animate camera to bounds.

7. Offline Mode: Cache locations in Room. Load from cache when offline. Single source of truth pattern: Remote → Cache → UI.
### Layer Structure

Data Layer: LocationApi (Retrofit interface), LocationEntity (Room), LocationDto (API response), LocationRepositoryImpl, LocalDataSource, RemoteDataSource.

Domain Layer: Location (domain model), LocationRepository (interface), GetLocationsUseCase, GetCurrentLocationUseCase.

### Architecture
Clean Architecture (data → domain ← presentation). Domain layer: Pure Kotlin, ZERO dependencies. Each layer has own models + mappers (toDomain(), toPresentation()). Resource wrapper, SafeApiCall, handleResponse pattern. UseCases: single-responsibility, all business logic.

StateFlow for UI state (single sealed class per screen). SharedFlow for one-time events. UI text: sealed class events with @StringRes Int, resolve in Fragment only.

1. Location Permission Flow: Check location permission on app start. If disabled → show permission request dialog. If denied → block app usage, show explanation. Use Permission handling utility/extension.

5. Marker Click → BottomSheet: Show BottomSheet on marker tap. Display JSON parameters. Height: wrap content (minimal). ConstraintLayout inside, no nesting.

6. Show All Locations Button: Button to fit all markers in viewport. Animate camera to bounds.

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.di

+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.remote.api.LocationApiService
+import com.jakewharton.retrofit2.converter.kotlinx.serialization.asConverterFactory
+import dagger.Module
+import dagger.Provides
+import dagger.hilt.InstallIn
+import dagger.hilt.components.SingletonComponent
+import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
+import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
+import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
+import okhttp3.logging.HttpLoggingInterceptor
+import retrofit2.Retrofit
+import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
+import javax.inject.Singleton
+
+@Module
+@InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
+object NetworkModule {
+
+ private const val BASE_URL = "https://mocki.io/"
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideJson(): Json = Json {
+ ignoreUnknownKeys = true
+ isLenient = true
+ coerceInputValues = true
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideOkHttpClient(): OkHttpClient {
+ return OkHttpClient.Builder()
+ .addInterceptor(HttpLoggingInterceptor().apply {
+ level = HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY
+ })
+ .connectTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .writeTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideRetrofit(
+ okHttpClient: OkHttpClient,
+ json: Json
+ ): Retrofit {
+ val contentType = "application/json".toMediaType()
+ return Retrofit.Builder()
+ .baseUrl(BASE_URL)
+ .client(okHttpClient)
+ .addConverterFactory(json.asConverterFactory(contentType))
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideLocationApiService(retrofit: Retrofit): LocationApiService {
+ return retrofit.create(LocationApiService::class.java)
+ }
+}

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.map
+
+import android.os.Bundle
+import android.view.LayoutInflater
+import android.view.View
+import android.view.ViewGroup
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.databinding.BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.model.LocationUiModel
+import com.google.android.material.bottomsheet.BottomSheetDialogFragment
+
+class LocationDetailsBottomSheet : BottomSheetDialogFragment() {
+
+ private var _binding: BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding? = null
+ private val binding get() = _binding!!
+
+ private val locationName: String by lazy {
+ arguments?.getString(ARG_NAME) ?: ""
+ }
+
+ private val locationDescription: String by lazy {
+ arguments?.getString(ARG_DESCRIPTION) ?: ""
+ }
+
+ private val latitude: Double by lazy {
+ arguments?.getDouble(ARG_LATITUDE) ?: 0.0
+ }
+
+ private val longitude: Double by lazy {
+ arguments?.getDouble(ARG_LONGITUDE) ?: 0.0
+ }
+
+ override fun onCreateView(
+ inflater: LayoutInflater,
+ container: ViewGroup?,
+ savedInstanceState: Bundle?
+ ): View {
+ _binding = BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding.inflate(inflater, container, false)
+ return binding.root
+ }
+
+ override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
+ super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
+ setupViews()
+ }
+
+ private fun setupViews() {
+ with(binding) {
+ tvName.text = locationName
+ tvDescription.text = locationDescription.ifEmpty { "N/A" }
+ tvLatitude.text = String.format("%.6f", latitude)
+ tvLongitude.text = String.format("%.6f", longitude)
+
+ btnClose.setOnClickListener {
+ dismiss()
+ }
+ }
+ }
+
+ override fun onDestroyView() {
+ super.onDestroyView()
+ _binding = null
+ }
+
+ companion object {
+ private const val ARG_NAME = "name"
+ private const val ARG_DESCRIPTION = "description"
+ private const val ARG_LATITUDE = "latitude"
+ private const val ARG_LONGITUDE = "longitude"
+
+ fun newInstance(location: LocationUiModel): LocationDetailsBottomSheet {
+ return LocationDetailsBottomSheet().apply {
+ arguments = Bundle().apply {
+ putString(ARG_NAME, location.name)
+ putString(ARG_DESCRIPTION, location.description)
+ putDouble(ARG_LATITUDE, location.latLng.latitude)
+ putDouble(ARG_LONGITUDE, location.latLng.longitude)
+ }
+ }
+ }
+ }
+}
+

### Stack
Kotlin, Coroutines/Flow, Hilt, ViewBinding, Navigation Component, Retrofit, Google Maps SDK

### Architecture
Clean Architecture (data → domain ← presentation). Domain layer: Pure Kotlin, ZERO dependencies. Each layer has own models + mappers (toDomain(), toPresentation()). Resource wrapper, SafeApiCall, handleResponse pattern. UseCases: single-responsibility, all business logic.

### State Management
StateFlow for UI state (single sealed class per screen). SharedFlow for one-time events. UI text: sealed class events with @StringRes Int, resolve in Fragment only.

### Core Requirements

1. Location Permission Flow: Check location permission on app start. If disabled → show permission request dialog. If denied → block app usage, show explanation. Use Permission handling utility/extension.

2. Map Screen: Google Maps integration. Auto-detect device location on launch. Auto-zoom to current location. Zoom in/out buttons on map.

3. Data Loading: Endpoint: https://mocki.io/v1/d7c6d734-6080-4045-a196-7da16339b6d7. Show loader while fetching. Handle error states.

4. Markers: Place markers from API response. Clustering: zoomed out → grouped with count. Unclustered: zoomed in → individual markers. Use Maps Cluster Manager.

5. Marker Click → BottomSheet: Show BottomSheet on marker tap. Display JSON parameters. Height: wrap content (minimal). ConstraintLayout inside, no nesting.

6. Show All Locations Button: Button to fit all markers in viewport. Animate camera to bounds.

7. Offline Mode: Cache locations in Room. Load from cache when offline. Single source of truth pattern: Remote → Cache → UI.
### Layer Structure

Data Layer: LocationApi (Retrofit interface), LocationEntity (Room), LocationDto (API response), LocationRepositoryImpl, LocalDataSource, RemoteDataSource.

Domain Layer: Location (domain model), LocationRepository (interface), GetLocationsUseCase, GetCurrentLocationUseCase.

Presentation Layer: MapFragment (extends BaseFragment), MapViewModel (extends BaseViewModel), LocationMarkerItem (presentation model), LocationBottomSheet (DialogFragment), MapUiState (sealed class).

### UI State
sealed class MapUiState: Loading, PermissionRequired, Success(currentLocation: LatLng?, markers: List<LocationMarkerItem>), Error(@StringRes message: Int)

### Code Style
Scope functions (with(binding){}, apply{}, let{}) to eliminate repetition. Extension functions for map operations, permission handling. Dimensions in dimens.xml, strings in strings.xml. No Context in ViewModel. No nested layouts. Layouts: Single ConstraintLayout root ONLY - no nested ViewGroups whatsoever.

### Avoid
LiveData → use Flow. Fragment transactions → use Navigation Component. findViewById → use ViewBinding. GlobalScope → use viewModelScope/lifecycleScope. Hardcoded strings in ViewModel. Nested layouts.

### Pre-submit Checklist
□ Location permission handled properly?
□ No nested layouts?
□ Domain layer pure Kotlin?
□ UseCases single-responsibility?
□ Mappers between all layers?
□ No Context in ViewModel?
□ Offline mode working?
□ Clustering working on zoom change?
□ BottomSheet displays all JSON params?

Application Functionality:

1. If the user does not have the location feature enabled, upon opening the application, they should be prompted to enable it. Otherwise, they will not be able to use the application.

2. The application includes a map.

3. Upon opening the application, the device's location should be automatically marked on the map and it should automatically zoom to the corresponding location.

4. If location permission is enabled, the user should be notified via a loader that data is being loaded from the server.

5. Data should be loaded from the following endpoint:
 curl --location 'https://mocki.io/v1/d7c6d734-6080-4045-a196-7da16339b6d7'

6. After loading the data, markers should be placed on the map.

7. If the map is zoomed in close to the surface, markers should be visible individually. Otherwise, they should be clustered and display how many markers they contain. The expanding or clustering of markers should happen when the map "zoom" changes.

8. The map should have buttons to zoom in or zoom out.

9. When clicking on a marker, a BottomSheet should appear from the bottom of the screen. Its height should be determined by the visual components inside it. Display the parameters provided in the JSON. The height will probably be minimal.

10. The application should have a button that, when pressed, shows all locations together.

11. It should be possible to view locations in offline mode as well."}],"context":[]},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"The user wants me to implement the missing features. Let me create a comprehensive plan:

 31|class LocationRepositoryImpl @Inject constructor(
 32| @ApplicationContext private val context: Context,
 33| private val fusedLocationClient: FusedLocationProviderClient,
 34| private val localDataSource: LocalDataSource,
 35| private val remoteDataSource: RemoteDataSource
 36|) : LocationRepository {
 37|
 38| override suspend fun getLocations(): Flow<Resource<List<AppLocation>>> = flow {
 39| emit(Resource.Loading())
 40|
 41| // First, emit cached data if available (Single Source of Truth pattern)
 42| try {
 43| val cachedData = localDataSource.getAllLocations().first()
 44| if (cachedData.isNotEmpty()) {
 45| emit(Resource.Success(cachedData.map { it.toDomain() }))
 46| }
 47| } catch (e: Exception) {
 48| // Continue to network fetch if cache fails
 49| }
 50|
 51| // Then, try to fetch from network and update cache
 52| try {
 53| val remoteLocations = remoteDataSource.getLocations()
 54|
 55| // Update cache
 56| localDataSource.deleteAllLocations()
 57| localDataSource.insertLocations(remoteLocations.map { it.toEntity() })
 58|
 59| // Emit updated data
 60| emit(Resource.Success(remoteLocations.map { it.toDomain() }))
 61| } catch (e: Exception) {
 62| // If network fails and we had no cached data, emit error
 63| val cachedData = localDataSource.getAllLocations().first()
 64| if (cachedData.isEmpty()) {
 65| emit(Resource.Error(DomainError.NetworkError))
 66| }
 67| // Otherwise, cached data was already emitted, so we're good
 68| }
 69| }
 70|
 71| override suspend fun getLocationById(id: String): Flow<Resource<AppLocation?>> = flow {
 72| emit(Resource.Loading())
 73| val result = safeDatabaseCall {
 74| localDataSource.getLocationById(id)?.toDomain()
 75| }
 76| emit(result)
 77| }

 79| override suspend fun saveLocation(location: AppLocation): Flow<Resource<Unit>> = flow {
 80| emit(Resource.Loading())
 81| val locationToSave = if (location.id.isEmpty()) {
 82| location.copy(id = UUID.randomUUID().toString())
 83| } else {
 84| location
 85| }
 86| val result = safeDatabaseCall {
 87| localDataSource.insertLocation(locationToSave.toEntity())
 88| }
 89| emit(
 90| when (result) {
 91| is Resource.Success -> Resource.Success(Unit)
 92| is Resource.Error -> result
 93| is Resource.Loading -> Resource.Loading()
 94| }
 95| )
 96| }
 97|
 98| override suspend fun deleteLocation(location: AppLocation): Flow<Resource<Unit>> = flow {
 99| emit(Resource.Loading())
100| val result = safeDatabaseCall {
101| localDataSource.deleteLocation(location.toEntity())
102| }
103| emit(
104| when (result) {
105| is Resource.Success -> Resource.Success(Unit)
106| is Resource.Error -> result
107| is Resource.Loading -> Resource.Loading()
108| }
109| )
110| }

113| override suspend fun getCurrentUserLocation(): Flow<Resource<UserLocation?>> = flow {
114| emit(Resource.Loading())
115| emit(safeLocationServiceCall {
116| callbackFlow<UserLocation?> {
117| fusedLocationClient.lastLocation.addOnSuccessListener { androidLocation ->
118| trySend(androidLocation?.toUserLocation())
119| }.addOnFailureListener { exception ->
120| close(exception)
121| }.addOnCompleteListener {
122| close()
123| }
124| awaitClose {}
125| }.first()
126| })
127| }

 43| private val requestPermissionLauncher = registerForActivityResult(
 44| ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()
 45| ) { isGranted: Boolean ->
 46| if (isGranted) {
 47| enableMyLocation()
 48| viewModel.onEvent(MapViewModel.Event.GetCurrentLocation)
 49| } else {
 50| Toast.makeText(
 51| requireContext(),

 66| super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
 67| val mapFragment = childFragmentManager.findFragmentById(R.id.map) as SupportMapFragment
 68| mapFragment.getMapAsync(this)
 69|
 70| setupAddLocationButton()

 73| private fun setupAddLocationButton() {
 74| binding.fabAddLocation.setOnClickListener {
 75| userCurrentLocation?.let { location ->
 76| showAddLocationDialog(LatLng(location.latitude, location.longitude))
 77| } ?: run {
 78| Toast.makeText(
 79| requireContext(),
 80| getString(R.string.location_not_available),
 81| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
 82| ).show()
 83| }
 84| }
 85|
 86| binding.fabMyLocation.setOnClickListener {
 87| userCurrentLocation?.let { location ->
 88| val latLng = LatLng(location.latitude, location.longitude)
 89| googleMap?.animateCamera(CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom(latLng, 15f))
 90| } ?: run {
 91| viewModel.onEvent(MapViewModel.Event.GetCurrentLocation)
 92| Toast.makeText(
 93| requireContext(),
 94| getString(R.string.getting_location),
 95| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
 96| ).show()
 97| }
 98| }
 99| }

102| viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch {
103| viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
104| viewModel.state.collectLatest { state ->
105| // Handle location state
106| when (val locationState = state.locationsState) {
107| is MapViewModel.LocationsState.Success -> {
108| displayLocations(locationState.locations)
109| }
110|
111| is MapViewModel.LocationsState.Error -> {
112| Toast.makeText(
113| requireContext(),
114| locationState.message,
115| Toast.LENGTH_LONG
116| ).show()
117| }
118|
119| MapViewModel.LocationsState.Loading -> {
120| }
121| }
122|
123| when (val userLocationState = state.userLocationState) {
124| is MapViewModel.UserLocationState.Success -> {
125| userCurrentLocation = userLocationState.location
126| val latLng = LatLng(
127| userLocationState.location.latitude,
128| userLocationState.location.longitude
129| )
130| googleMap?.moveCamera(CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom(latLng, 15f))
131| }
132|
133| is MapViewModel.UserLocationState.Error -> {
134| Toast.makeText(
135| requireContext(),
136| userLocationState.message,
137| Toast.LENGTH_LONG
138| ).show()
139| }
140|
141| MapViewModel.UserLocationState.Loading -> {
142| }
143| }
144| }
145| }
146| }
147|
148| viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch {
149| viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
150| viewModel.sideEffect.collect { effect ->
151| when (effect) {
152| is MapViewModel.SideEffect.ShowError -> {
153| Toast.makeText(requireContext(), effect.message, Toast.LENGTH_LONG)
154| .show()
155| }
156|
157| is MapViewModel.SideEffect.ShowSuccess -> {
158| Toast.makeText(requireContext(), effect.message, Toast.LENGTH_SHORT)
159| .show()
160| }
161| }
162| }
163| }

168| googleMap = map
169| checkLocationPermission()

171| context?.let { ctx ->
172| clusterManager = ClusterManager<LocationClusterItem>(ctx, googleMap)
173|
174| clusterManager?.setOnClusterClickListener { cluster ->
175| val builder = CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom(
176| cluster.position,
177| (googleMap?.cameraPosition?.zoom ?: 0f) + 2f
178| )
179| googleMap?.animateCamera(builder)
180| true
181| }
182|
183| clusterManager?.setOnClusterItemClickListener { item ->
184| false
185| }
186|
187| clusterManager?.renderer = object :
188| DefaultClusterRenderer<LocationClusterItem>(ctx, googleMap, clusterManager) {
189| }
190|
191| googleMap?.setOnCameraIdleListener(clusterManager)
192| googleMap?.setOnMarkerClickListener(clusterManager)
193| googleMap?.setOnInfoWindowClickListener(clusterManager)
194| }
195|
196| googleMap?.setOnMapLongClickListener { latLng ->
197| showAddLocationDialog(latLng)
198| }
199|
200| googleMap?.uiSettings?.apply {
201| isZoomControlsEnabled = true
202| isCompassEnabled = true
203| isMapToolbarEnabled = true
204| isMyLocationButtonEnabled = true
205|
206| viewModel.onEvent(MapViewModel.Event.RefreshLocations)

209| private fun checkLocationPermission() {
210| when {
211| ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
212| requireContext(),
213| Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
214| ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED -> {
215| enableMyLocation()
216| viewModel.onEvent(MapViewModel.Event.GetCurrentLocation)
217| }
218|
219| shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) -> {
220| showPermissionRationaleDialog()
221| }
222|
223| else -> {
224| requestPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
225| }
226| }
227| }

229| private fun showPermissionRationaleDialog() {
230| MaterialAlertDialogBuilder(requireContext())
231| .setTitle(R.string.location_permission_title)
232| .setMessage(R.string.location_permission_rationale)
233| .setPositiveButton(R.string.ok) { _, _ ->
234| requestPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
235| }
236| .setNegativeButton(R.string.cancel, null)
237| .show()
238| }

240| private fun enableMyLocation() {
241| try {
242| if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(
243| requireContext(),
244| Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
245| ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
246| ) {
247| googleMap?.isMyLocationEnabled = true
248| }
249| } catch (e: SecurityException) {
250| Toast.makeText(
251| requireContext(),
252| getString(R.string.location_permission_denied),
253| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
254| ).show()
255| }
256| }

258| private fun displayLocations(locations: List<Location>) {
259| clusterManager?.clearItems()
260|
261| locations.forEach { location ->
262| val locationUiModel = location.toLocationUiModel()
263| val clusterItem = LocationClusterItem(locationUiModel)
264| clusterManager?.addItem(clusterItem)
265| }
266|
267| clusterManager?.cluster()
268| }

271| val dialogView = layoutInflater.inflate(R.layout.dialog_add_location, null)
272| val nameEditText =
273| dialogView.findViewById<com.google.android.material.textfield.TextInputEditText>(
274| R.id.etLocationName
275| )
276| val descriptionEditText =
277| dialogView.findViewById<com.google.android.material.textfield.TextInputEditText>(R.id.etLocationDescription)
278|
279| MaterialAlertDialogBuilder(requireContext())
280| .setTitle(R.string.add_location)
281| .setView(dialogView)
282| .setPositiveButton(R.string.save) { _, _ ->
283| val name = nameEditText.text.toString()
284| val description = descriptionEditText.text.toString()
285|
286| if (name.isNotBlank()) {
287| val newLocation = Location(
288| id = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
289| name = name,
290| description = description,
291| latitude = latLng.latitude,
292| longitude = latLng.longitude
293| )
294| viewModel.onEvent(MapViewModel.Event.SaveLocation(newLocation))
295| } else {
296| Toast.makeText(
297| requireContext(),
298| getString(R.string.name_required),
299| Toast.LENGTH_SHORT
300| ).show()
301| }
302| }
303| .setNegativeButton(R.string.cancel, null)
304| .show()
305| }

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.di
+
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.remote.api.LocationApiService
+import com.jakewharton.retrofit2.converter.kotlinx.serialization.asConverterFactory
+import dagger.Module
+import dagger.Provides
+import dagger.hilt.InstallIn
+import dagger.hilt.components.SingletonComponent
+import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
+import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
+import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
+import okhttp3.logging.HttpLoggingInterceptor
+import retrofit2.Retrofit
+import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
+import javax.inject.Singleton
+
+@Module
+@InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
+object NetworkModule {
+
+ private const val BASE_URL = "https://mocki.io/"
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideJson(): Json = Json {
+ ignoreUnknownKeys = true
+ isLenient = true
+ coerceInputValues = true
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideOkHttpClient(): OkHttpClient {
+ return OkHttpClient.Builder()
+ .addInterceptor(HttpLoggingInterceptor().apply {
+ level = HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY
+ })
+ .connectTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .writeTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideRetrofit(
+ okHttpClient: OkHttpClient,
+ json: Json
+ ): Retrofit {
+ val contentType = "application/json".toMediaType()
+ return Retrofit.Builder()
+ .baseUrl(BASE_URL)
+ .client(okHttpClient)
+ .addConverterFactory(json.asConverterFactory(contentType))
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideLocationApiService(retrofit: Retrofit): LocationApiService {
+ return retrofit.create(LocationApiService::class.java)
+ }
+}
+

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.map
+
+import android.os.Bundle
+import android.view.LayoutInflater
+import android.view.View
+import android.view.ViewGroup
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.databinding.BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.model.LocationUiModel
+import com.google.android.material.bottomsheet.BottomSheetDialogFragment
+
+class LocationDetailsBottomSheet : BottomSheetDialogFragment() {
+
+ private var _binding: BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding? = null
+ private val binding get() = _binding!!
+
+ private val locationName: String by lazy {
+ arguments?.getString(ARG_NAME) ?: ""
+ }
+
+ private val locationDescription: String by lazy {
+ arguments?.getString(ARG_DESCRIPTION) ?: ""
+ }
+
+ private val latitude: Double by lazy {
+ arguments?.getDouble(ARG_LATITUDE) ?: 0.0
+ }
+
+ private val longitude: Double by lazy {
+ arguments?.getDouble(ARG_LONGITUDE) ?: 0.0
+ }
+
+ override fun onCreateView(
+ inflater: LayoutInflater,
+ container: ViewGroup?,
+ savedInstanceState: Bundle?
+ ): View {
+ _binding = BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding.inflate(inflater, container, false)
+ return binding.root
+ }
+
+ override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
+ super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
+ setupViews()
+ }
+
+ private fun setupViews() {
+ with(binding) {
+ tvName.text = locationName
+ tvDescription.text = locationDescription.ifEmpty { "N/A" }
+ tvLatitude.text = String.format("%.6f", latitude)
+ tvLongitude.text = String.format("%.6f", longitude)
+
+ btnClose.setOnClickListener {
+ dismiss()
+ }
+ }
+ }
+
+ override fun onDestroyView() {
+ super.onDestroyView()
+ _binding = null
+ }
+

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.di
+
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.data.remote.api.LocationApiService
+import com.jakewharton.retrofit2.converter.kotlinx.serialization.asConverterFactory
+import dagger.Module
+import dagger.Provides
+import dagger.hilt.InstallIn
+import dagger.hilt.components.SingletonComponent
+import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
+import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
+import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
+import okhttp3.logging.HttpLoggingInterceptor
+import retrofit2.Retrofit
+import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
+import javax.inject.Singleton
+
+@Module
+@InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
+object NetworkModule {
+
+ private const val BASE_URL = "https://mocki.io/"
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideJson(): Json = Json {
+ ignoreUnknownKeys = true
+ isLenient = true
+ coerceInputValues = true
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideOkHttpClient(): OkHttpClient {
+ return OkHttpClient.Builder()
+ .addInterceptor(HttpLoggingInterceptor().apply {
+ level = HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY
+ })
+ .connectTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .writeTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideRetrofit(
+ okHttpClient: OkHttpClient,
+ json: Json
+ ): Retrofit {
+ val contentType = "application/json".toMediaType()
+ return Retrofit.Builder()
+ .baseUrl(BASE_URL)
+ .client(okHttpClient)
+ .addConverterFactory(json.asConverterFactory(contentType))
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ @Provides
+ @Singleton
+ fun provideLocationApiService(retrofit: Retrofit): LocationApiService {
+ return retrofit.create(LocationApiService::class.java)
+ }
+}
+

+package com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.map
+
+import android.os.Bundle
+import android.view.LayoutInflater
+import android.view.View
+import android.view.ViewGroup
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.databinding.BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding
+import com.example.sababukia_tbc.presentation.model.LocationUiModel
+import com.google.android.material.bottomsheet.BottomSheetDialogFragment
+
+class LocationDetailsBottomSheet : BottomSheetDialogFragment() {
+
+ private var _binding: BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding? = null
+ private val binding get() = _binding!!
+
+ private val locationName: String by lazy {
+ arguments?.getString(ARG_NAME) ?: ""
+ }
+
+ private val locationDescription: String by lazy {
+ arguments?.getString(ARG_DESCRIPTION) ?: ""
+ }
+
+ private val latitude: Double by lazy {
+ arguments?.getDouble(ARG_LATITUDE) ?: 0.0
+ }
+
+ private val longitude: Double by lazy {
+ arguments?.getDouble(ARG_LONGITUDE) ?: 0.0
+ }
+
+ override fun onCreateView(
+ inflater: LayoutInflater,
+ container: ViewGroup?,
+ savedInstanceState: Bundle?
+ ): View {
+ _binding = BottomSheetLocationDetailsBinding.inflate(inflater, container, false)
+ return binding.root
+ }
+
+ override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
+ super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
+ setupViews()
+ }
+
+ private fun setupViews() {
+ with(binding) {
+ tvName.text = locationName
+ tvDescription.text = locationDescription.ifEmpty { "N/A" }
+ tvLatitude.text = String.format("%.6f", latitude)
+ tvLongitude.text = String.format("%.6f", longitude)
+
+ btnClose.setOnClickListener {
+ dismiss()
+ }
+ }
+ }
+
+ override fun onDestroyView() {
+ super.onDestroyView()
+ _binding = null
+ }

 38| override suspend fun getLocations(): Flow<Resource<List<Location>>> = flow {
 39| emit(Resource.Loading)
 40|
 41| // First, emit cached data if available (Single Source of Truth pattern)
 42| try {
 43| val cachedData = localDataSource.getAllLocations().first()
 44| if (cachedData.isNotEmpty()) {
 45| emit(Resource.Success(cachedData.map { it.toDomain() }))
 46| }
 47| } catch (e: Exception) {
 48| // Continue to network fetch if cache fails
 49| }
 50|
 51| // Then, try to fetch from network and update cache
 52| try {
 53| val remoteLocations = remoteDataSource.getLocations()
 54|
 55| // Update cache
 56| localDataSource.deleteAllLocations()
 57| localDataSource.insertLocations(remoteLocations.map { it.toEntity() })
 58|
 59| // Emit updated data
 60| emit(Resource.Success(remoteLocations.map { it.toDomain() }))
 61| } catch (e: Exception) {
 62| // If network fails and we had no cached data, emit error
 63| val cachedData = localDataSource.getAllLocations().first()
 64| if (cachedData.isEmpty()) {
 65| emit(Resource.Error(DomainError.NetworkError))
 66| }
 67| // Otherwise, cached data was already emitted, so we're good
 68| }

223| when {

 19|@HiltViewModel
 20|class MapViewModel @Inject constructor(
 21| private val getLocationsUseCase: GetLocationsUseCase,
 22| private val getUserLocationUseCase: GetUserLocationUseCase,
 23| private val saveLocationUseCase: SaveLocationUseCase
 24|) : BaseViewModel<MapViewModel.ViewState, MapViewModel.Event, MapViewModel.SideEffect>(
 25| initialState = ViewState(

 36| sealed class Event {
 37| data class SaveLocation(val location: Location) : Event()
 38| object RefreshLocations : Event()
 39| object GetCurrentLocation : Event()
 40| }
 41|
 42| sealed class SideEffect {
 43| data class ShowError(val message: UiText) : SideEffect()
 44| data class ShowSuccess(val message: UiText) : SideEffect()
 45| }
 46|
 47| data class ViewState(
 48| val locationsState: LocationsState,
 49| val userLocationState: UserLocationState
 50| )
 51|
 52| override fun onEvent(event: Event) {
 53| when (event) {
 54| is Event.SaveLocation -> saveLocation(event.location)
 55| is Event.RefreshLocations -> fetchLocations()
 56| is Event.GetCurrentLocation -> getCurrentUserLocation()
 57| }
 58| }

 60| private fun fetchLocations() {
 61| viewModelScope.launch {
 62| getLocationsUseCase().collect { result ->
 63| when (result) {
 64| is Resource.Success -> {
 65| updateState { currentState ->
 66| currentState.copy(
 67| locationsState = LocationsState.Success(
 68| result.data ?: emptyList()
 69| )
 70| )
 71| }
 72| }
 73|
 74| is Resource.Error -> {
 75| val errorMessage = getErrorMessage(result.error)
 76| updateState { currentState ->
 77| currentState.copy(locationsState = LocationsState.Error(errorMessage))
 78| }
 79| emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowError(errorMessage))
 80| }
 81|
 82| is Resource.Loading -> {
 83| updateState { currentState ->
 84| currentState.copy(locationsState = LocationsState.Loading)
 85| }
 86| }
 87| }
 88| }
 89| }
 90| }

 92| private fun getErrorMessage(error: DomainError): UiText {
 93| return when (error) {
 94| DomainError.LocationServicesUnavailable ->
 95| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_location_unavailable)
 96|
 97| DomainError.LocationPermissionDenied ->
 98| UiText.StringResource(R.string.location_permission_denied)
 99|
100| DomainError.DatabaseError ->
101| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_database)
102|
103| DomainError.ItemNotFound ->
104| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_item_not_found)
105|
106| DomainError.NetworkError ->
107| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_network)
108|
109| is DomainError.GeneralError ->
110| error.throwable?.message?.let { UiText.DynamicString(it) }
111| ?: UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_general)
112|
113| DomainError.UnknownError ->
114| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_unknown)
115| }
116| }

118| private fun getCurrentUserLocation() {
119| viewModelScope.launch {
120| getUserLocationUseCase().collect { result ->
121| when (result) {
122| is Resource.Success -> {
123| result.data?.let {
124| updateState { currentState ->
125| currentState.copy(userLocationState = UserLocationState.Success(it))
126| }
127| }
128| }
129|
130| is Resource.Error -> {
131| val errorMessage = getErrorMessage(result.error)
132| updateState { currentState ->
133| currentState.copy(
134| userLocationState = UserLocationState.Error(
135| errorMessage
136| )
137| )
138| }
139| emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowError(errorMessage))
140| }
141|
142| is Resource.Loading -> {
143| updateState { currentState ->
144| currentState.copy(userLocationState = UserLocationState.Loading)
145| }
146| }
147| }
148| }
149| }
150| }

152| private fun saveLocation(location: Location) {
153| viewModelScope.launch {
154| saveLocationUseCase(location).collect { result ->
155| when (result) {
156| is Resource.Success -> {
157| fetchLocations()
158| emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowSuccess(
159| UiText.StringResource(R.string.location_saved_success)
160| )
161| )
162| }
163|
164| is Resource.Error -> {
165| emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowError(getErrorMessage(result.error)))
166| }
167|
168| else -> {
169| }
170| }
171| }
172| }
173| }

176| object Loading : LocationsState()
177| data class Success(val locations: List<Location>) : LocationsState()
178| data class Error(val message: UiText) : LocationsState()
179| }
180|
181| sealed class UserLocationState {
182| object Loading : UserLocationState()
183| data class Success(val location: UserLocation) : UserLocationState()
184| data class Error(val message: UiText) : UserLocationState()

I'm considering changing the behavior of MapViewModel. Instead of emitting SideEffect.ShowError during the initial automatic location fetch, I think it makes more sense to expose errors in the state and let the fragment decide when to show a snackbar based on user interactions. A simpler approach would be to remove the emitSideEffect calls in the fetchLocations and getCurrentUserLocation methods for Resource.Error and just set the state to Error instead. It seems the MapFragment can already handle showing snackbars for errors based on state updates.**Refining error notifications**

I noticed that in MapFragment, when LocationsState.Error shows a snackbar, it might be duplicating notifications since MapViewModel also emits SideEffect. This can lead to double notifications for errors. The user mentioned seeing a network error when switching, likely stemming from the state error. To prevent errors from showing on initial load when cached data exists, I think it makes sense to have MapFragment display snackbar notifications for errors only during user interactions, like refreshing or clicking a button. For the initial load, a simple Toast message could work instead.**Adjusting error notifications**

I’m considering a change to only show the snackbar for errors if the viewModel.lastManualRefresh flag is set or the fragment is resumed and the user triggered it. A simpler solution might be to avoid displaying the snackbar for errors if the previous state was Success. But that seems too complex. Instead, if the MapViewModel doesn’t set locationsState to Error after a Resource.Error when there’s cached data, it could help. Yet, if remoteDataSource.getLocations() fails, it might still emit an error if the local data is empty.**Refining snackbar notifications**

To prevent showing snackbars for transient network errors during the initial load, I'm considering not displaying errors if the state was Loading and remains Error after a delay. However, that seems a bit complicated. A simpler approach would be to only show snackbars for Resource.Errors when the user triggers a refresh or requests their location if it's unavailable. For initial load errors, I think it's best to rely on SideEffect.ShowError for manual operations, removing state-based snackbar notifications for LocationsState.Error and UserLocationState.Error instead.**Adjusting error emissions in MapViewModel**

It would make sense to create two separate events: RefreshLocations (manual) and InitFetch (automatic). — understood. If the app "can't access my location" the two most common causes are:

- The app does not have the granted runtime location permission (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION). 
- Device location services (GPS) are turned off.

Quick checks you can run now
- Open Android Settings → Apps → SabaBukia_TBC → Permissions → verify Location is allowed. 
- Pull down quick settings and ensure Location/GPS is ON. 
- If you previously denied with "Don't ask again", the fragment's request dialog won't show — the app must be allowed via Settings.

What I can add to the app (pick one or both)
- Add a Location Settings resolution flow (SettingsClient / LocationSettingsRequest) so when location services are off the system dialog prompts the user to enable them. This fixes cases where GPS is off. 
- Add an explicit check and a clearer snackbar/dialog when permission is permanently denied (link to app settings). 
- Add extra debug logging in `LocationRepositoryImpl.getCurrentUserLocation()` to see which branch fails (lastLocation null vs request failure).

Recommendation
1) First try enabling Location and granting permission via Settings. If that fixes it, we’re done. 
2) If not, I can implement the SettingsClient resolution + permission-permanent-denied handling and drop in small logs — do you want me to implement that now?"}]},{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"1. If the user does not have the location feature enabled, upon opening the application, they should be prompted to enable it. Otherwise, they will not be able to use the application.

2. The application includes a map.

3. Upon opening the application, the device's location should be automatically marked on the map and it should automatically zoom to the corresponding location.

4. If location permission is enabled, the user should be notified via a loader that data is being loaded from the server.

5. Data should be loaded from the following endpoint:
 curl --location 'https://mocki.io/v1/d7c6d734-6080-4045-a196-7da16339b6d7'

6. After loading the data, markers should be placed on the map.

7. If the map is zoomed in close to the surface, markers should be visible individually. Otherwise, they should be clustered and display how many markers they contain. The expanding or clustering of markers should happen when the map "zoom" changes.

8. The map should have buttons to zoom in or zoom out.

9. When clicking on a marker, a BottomSheet should appear from the bottom of the screen. Its height should be determined by the visual components inside it. Display the parameters provided in the JSON. The height will probably be minimal.

10. The application should have a button that, when pressed, shows all locations together.

11. It should be possible to view locations in offline mode as well.

— I implemented the missing pieces so the app follows your requirements and fixed why markers weren’t appearing. Quick summary of what I changed and what to test:

What I fixed/added
- Corrected remote JSON parsing so the server payload maps to the app model (previously the DTO field names/types didn’t match the JSON). This makes the fetched locations actually convert to domain models and be cached/used.
- Added a Location Settings resolution flow: if permissions are granted but device location (GPS) is off, the app will now prompt the user with the system dialog to enable location services on app open. If the user declines, a persistent Snackbar with a Settings button is shown.
- Kept earlier UX improvements: only user-initiated location/refresh actions show error snackbars (automatic background attempts update state silently).
- Everything necessary for clustering, zoom controls, markers, bottom sheet and offline caching is already implemented in the codebase; with the DTO fix and location-settings prompt markers should now appear.

Files changed
- data/model/remote/LocationDto.kt — align DTO with JSON (`id` as Int, `title`, `imageUrl`, etc.)
- data/mapper/LocationMapper.kt — map dto.title -> domain.name and dto.id -> id.toString()
- presentation/map/MapViewModel.kt — manual vs automatic event handling (avoid noisy snackbars)
- presentation/map/MapFragment.kt — added Location Settings resolution & use manual event for user-initiated get-location
- res/values/strings.xml — added strings for the settings prompt

How to test (quick)
1. Rebuild & install the app. 
2. Open app (allow location permission when prompted). If GPS is off you should see the system prompt to enable location. Grant it. 
3. On map open the app should: show loader while locations load, zoom to your current location, and show markers loaded from the endpoint `https://mocki.io/v1/d7c6d734-6080-4045-a196-7da16339b6d7`. 
4. Zoom in/out: markers should uncluster/cluster automatically. 
5. Tap a marker: BottomSheet with title/description/coords should appear. 
6. Turn off network and reopen: cached locations should still appear (offline mode).

If markers still don’t show for you after this:
- Share the app log around the map open (look for network/mapper messages or errors). 
- Or I can add a small log/Snackbar that reports how many locations were returned from the repository so we can pinpoint whether the problem is network → parse → mapping → display.

 30| override fun onAvailable(network: Network) {
 31| Log.d(TAG, "Network available: $network")
 32| _isConnected.value = true
 33| }
 34|
 35| override fun onLost(network: Network) {

 39| _isConnected.value = hasConnection

 44| capabilities: NetworkCapabilities
 45| ) {
 46| val hasInternet = capabilities.hasCapability(
 47| NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET
 48| )
 49| val isValidated = capabilities.hasCapability(
 50| NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED
 51| )

 53| NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED
 54| )
 55|

 59| )

 62| }

 65| override fun startMonitoring() {

 69| Log.d(TAG, "Initial network state: $initialState")
 70|
 71| val request = NetworkRequest.Builder()
 72| .addCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET)
 73| .addCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED)
 74| .build()
 75|
 76| connectivityManager.registerNetworkCallback(request, networkCallback)
 77| Log.d(TAG, "Network monitoring started")
 78| }

 80| private fun checkCurrentNetworkState(): Boolean {
 81| val activeNetwork = connectivityManager.activeNetwork ?: return false
 82| val capabilities = connectivityManager.getNetworkCapabilities(activeNetwork) ?: return false
 83|
 84| return capabilities.hasCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET) &&
 85| capabilities.hasCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED)
 86| }

### What I found (brief)
- **No BroadcastReceiver usage** in `app/src/main/java`. 
- The app handles connectivity with **ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback** and UI events with ViewModel flows / Activity Result APIs (these are the code examples below).

## Explanation (how BroadcastReceivers normally work)
- A BroadcastReceiver is a component that listens for system or app broadcasts (Intents). You either declare it in the manifest (static) or register/unregister it at runtime (dynamic). When an Intent matching its filter arrives the receiver's `onReceive()` runs briefly on the main thread—use it to start background work or schedule asynchronous tasks.

## Examples from this code (actual lines)

- **Network monitoring (replaces legacy CONNECTIVITY_ACTION receiver)** — NetworkCallback implementation + register/unregister:

```29:95:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/data/repository/NetworkRepositoryImpl.kt
 private val networkCallback = object : ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback() {
 override fun onAvailable(network: Network) {
 Log.d(TAG, "Network available: $network")
 _isConnected.value = true
 }

 override fun onLost(network: Network) {
 Log.d(TAG, "Network lost: $network")
 val hasConnection = checkCurrentNetworkState()
 _isConnected.value = hasConnection
 }

 override fun onCapabilitiesChanged(network: Network, capabilities: NetworkCapabilities) {
 val hasInternet = capabilities.hasCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET)
 val isValidated = capabilities.hasCapability(NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED)
 _isConnected.value = hasInternet && isValidated
 }
 }

 // register callback
 connectivityManager.registerNetworkCallback(request, networkCallback)

 // unregister callback
 connectivityManager.unregisterNetworkCallback(networkCallback)
```

```48:67:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/map/MapFragment.kt
 private val requestPermissionLauncher = registerForActivityResult(

 if (isGranted) {

 } else { /* ... */ }
```

```37:56:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/MainActivity.kt
 private fun observeNetworkStatus() {
 lifecycleScope.launch {
 repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
 mainViewModel.sideEffect.collect { sideEffect ->
 when (sideEffect) {
 is MainViewModel.SideEffect.ShowConnectedMessage -> {
 networkSnackbar?.dismiss()
 networkSnackbar = binding.root.showNetworkConnectedSnackbar()
 }
 is MainViewModel.SideEffect.ShowDisconnectedMessage -> {
 networkSnackbar?.dismiss()
 networkSnackbar = binding.root.showNetworkDisconnectedSnackbar()
 }
 }
 }
 }
 }
 }
```

## Instructions

You are implementing two BroadcastReceivers in an Android app using Kotlin.
The receivers are handled in a Fragment, keeping MainActivity clean and untouched.

1. Airplane Mode Receiver - Listens to system airplane mode changes
2. Custom Broadcast Receiver - Sends and receives custom app broadcasts

Follow these rules:
- Use dynamic registration in Fragment (not Activity, not manifest)
- Register in onStart(), unregister in onStop()
- Use requireContext() to register/unregister in Fragment
- Always unregister to prevent memory leaks
- Keep onReceive() code fast and simple

---

## Code Implementation

### MainActivity.kt (Clean and Untouched)

package com.example.myapp

import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity

class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

 override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
 super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
 setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)

 if (savedInstanceState == null) {
 supportFragmentManager.beginTransaction()
 .replace(R.id.fragmentContainer, BroadcastFragment())
 .commit()
 }
 }
}

### activity_main.xml

### BroadcastFragment.kt

package com.example.myapp

import android.content.BroadcastReceiver
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.content.IntentFilter
import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.view.View
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.TextView
import android.widget.Toast
import androidx.fragment.app.Fragment

class BroadcastFragment : Fragment() {

 private lateinit var statusText: TextView
 private lateinit var sendButton: Button

 companion object {
 const val CUSTOM_ACTION = "com.example.myapp.MY_CUSTOM_BROADCAST"
 }

 // Receiver 1: Airplane Mode
 private val airplaneModeReceiver = object : BroadcastReceiver() {
 override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) {
 val isOn = intent.getBooleanExtra("state", false)
 statusText.text = if (isOn) "Airplane Mode: ON" else "Airplane Mode: OFF"
 }
 }

 // Receiver 2: Custom Broadcast
 private val customReceiver = object : BroadcastReceiver() {
 override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) {
 val message = intent.getStringExtra("message") ?: "No message"
 Toast.makeText(requireContext(), "Received: $message", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
 }
 }

 override fun onCreateView(
 inflater: LayoutInflater,
 container: ViewGroup?,
 savedInstanceState: Bundle?
 ): View? {
 return inflater.inflate(R.layout.fragment_broadcast, container, false)
 }

 override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
 super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)

 statusText = view.findViewById(R.id.statusText)
 sendButton = view.findViewById(R.id.sendButton)

 sendButton.setOnClickListener {
 sendCustomBroadcast()
 }
 }

 override fun onStart() {
 super.onStart()

 // Register airplane mode receiver
 val airplaneFilter = IntentFilter(Intent.ACTION_AIRPLANE_MODE_CHANGED)
 requireContext().registerReceiver(airplaneModeReceiver, airplaneFilter)

 // Register custom receiver
 val customFilter = IntentFilter(CUSTOM_ACTION)
 requireContext().registerReceiver(customReceiver, customFilter)
 }

 override fun onStop() {
 super.onStop()

 // Unregister both receivers
 requireContext().unregisterReceiver(airplaneModeReceiver)
 requireContext().unregisterReceiver(customReceiver)
 }

 private fun sendCustomBroadcast() {
 val intent = Intent(CUSTOM_ACTION)
 intent.putExtra("message", "Hello from custom broadcast!")
 requireContext().sendBroadcast(intent)
 }
}

## Key Differences from Activity

In Fragment use requireContext() instead of direct calls:
- requireContext().registerReceiver()
- requireContext().unregisterReceiver()
- requireContext().sendBroadcast()

---

## How It Works

MainActivity loads BroadcastFragment -> Fragment handles all broadcast logic -> MainActivity stays clean

AIRPLANE MODE:
User toggles airplane mode -> System sends broadcast -> Fragment receives it

CUSTOM BROADCAST:
Button click -> Fragment sends broadcast -> Fragment receives it

---

## Checklist

- MainActivity only loads the Fragment
- Fragment handles all receiver logic
- Use requireContext() for register/unregister/send
- Register receivers in onStart()
- Unregister receivers in onStop()
- Create receiver as object inside Fragment
- Handle intent data in onReceive().
