{\n return inflater.inflate(\n com.example.sababukia_tbc.R.layout.fragment_broadcast,\n container,\n false\n )\n }\n\n override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {\n super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)\n\n statusText = view.findViewById(com.example.sababukia_tbc.R.id.statusText)\n sendButton = view.findViewById(com.example.sababukia_tbc.R.id.sendButton)\n\n sendButton.setOnClickListener {\n sendCustomBroadcast()\n }\n }\n\n override fun onStart() {\n super.onStart()\n\n // Register airplane mode receiver (dynamic)\n val airplaneFilter = IntentFilter(Intent.ACTION_AIRPLANE_MODE_CHANGED)\n requireContext().registerReceiver(airplaneModeReceiver, airplaneFilter)\n\n // Register custom receiver\n val customFilter = IntentFilter(CUSTOM_ACTION)\n requireContext().registerReceiver(customReceiver, customFilter)\n }\n\n override fun onStop() {\n super.onStop()\n\n // Always unregister to prevent leaks; guard with try/catch\n try {\n requireContext().unregisterReceiver(airplaneModeReceiver)\n } catch (ignored: IllegalArgumentException) {\n }\n\n try {\n requireContext().unregisterReceiver(customReceiver)\n } catch (ignored: IllegalArgumentException) {\n }\n }\n\n private fun sendCustomBroadcast() {\n val intent = Intent(CUSTOM_ACTION)\n intent.putExtra(\"message\", \"Hello from custom broadcast!\")\n requireContext().sendBroadcast(intent)\n }\n}\n"}"}}]},{"role":"tool","name":"write","tool_call_id":"call_SIx9Q2TIonUhURfCB7hfqC5b","content":"Successfully created file at D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/broadcast/BroadcastFragment.kt

 38| override suspend fun getLocations(): Flow<Resource<List<Location>>> = flow {

 43| if (cachedData.isNotEmpty()) {
 44| emit(Resource.Success(cachedData.map { it.toDomain() }))

 47| }
 48|
 49| try {

 51|

 55| emit(Resource.Success(remoteLocations.map { it.toDomain() }))
 56| } catch (e: Exception) {

 76| } else {
 77| location

 81| }
 82| emit(

 87| }
 88| )

114| val locationRequest = LocationRequest.Builder(
115| Priority.PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY,
116| 10000L
117| ).setMaxUpdates(1).build()
118|
119| val locationCallback = object : LocationCallback() {
120| override fun onLocationResult(result: LocationResult) {
121| result.lastLocation?.let {
122| trySend(Resource.Success(it.toUserLocation()))
123| } ?: trySend(Resource.Error(DomainError.LocationServicesUnavailable))

132| }
133| }

 19|@HiltViewModel
 20|class MapViewModel @Inject constructor(
 21| private val getLocationsUseCase: GetLocationsUseCase,
 22| private val getUserLocationUseCase: GetUserLocationUseCase,
 23| private val saveLocationUseCase: SaveLocationUseCase
 24|) : BaseViewModel<MapViewModel.ViewState, MapViewModel.Event, MapViewModel.SideEffect>(
 25| initialState = ViewState(
 26| locationsState = LocationsState.Loading,
 27| userLocationState = UserLocationState.Loading
 28| )
 29|) {
 30|
 31| init {
 32| fetchLocations()
 33| getCurrentUserLocation()
 34| }
 35|
 36| sealed class Event {
 37| data class SaveLocation(val location: Location) : Event()
 38| object RefreshLocations : Event()
 39| object RefreshLocationsManual : Event()
 40| object GetCurrentLocation : Event()
 41| object GetCurrentLocationManual : Event()
 42| }
 43|
 44| sealed class SideEffect {
 45| data class ShowError(val message: UiText) : SideEffect()
 46| data class ShowSuccess(val message: UiText) : SideEffect()
 47| }
 48|
 49| data class ViewState(
 50| val locationsState: LocationsState,
 51| val userLocationState: UserLocationState
 52| )
 53|
 54| override fun onEvent(event: Event) {
 55| when (event) {
 56| is Event.SaveLocation -> saveLocation(event.location)
 57| is Event.RefreshLocations -> fetchLocations(manual = false)
 58| is Event.RefreshLocationsManual -> fetchLocations(manual = true)
 59| is Event.GetCurrentLocation -> getCurrentUserLocation(manual = false)
 60| is Event.GetCurrentLocationManual -> getCurrentUserLocation(manual = true)
 61| }
 62| }
 63|
 64| private fun fetchLocations(manual: Boolean = false) {
 65| viewModelScope.launch {
 66| getLocationsUseCase().collect { result ->
 67| when (result) {
 68| is Resource.Success -> {
 69| updateState { currentState ->
 70| currentState.copy(
 71| locationsState = LocationsState.Success(
 72| result.data ?: emptyList()
 73| )
 74| )
 75| }
 76| }
 77|
 78| is Resource.Error -> {
 79| val errorMessage = getErrorMessage(result.error)
 80| updateState { currentState ->
 81| currentState.copy(locationsState = LocationsState.Error(errorMessage))
 82| }
 83| if (manual) emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowError(errorMessage))
 84| }
 85|
 86| is Resource.Loading -> {
 87| updateState { currentState ->
 88| currentState.copy(locationsState = LocationsState.Loading)
 89| }
 90| }
 91| }
 92| }
 93| }
 94| }

 96| private fun getErrorMessage(error: DomainError): UiText {
 97| return when (error) {
 98| DomainError.LocationServicesUnavailable ->
 99| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_location_unavailable)
100|
101| DomainError.LocationPermissionDenied ->
102| UiText.StringResource(R.string.location_permission_denied)
103|

106|

108| UiText.StringResource(R.string.error_item_not_found)

122| private fun getCurrentUserLocation(manual: Boolean = false) {
123| viewModelScope.launch {
124| getUserLocationUseCase().collect { result ->
125| when (result) {
126| is Resource.Success -> {
127| result.data?.let {
128| updateState { currentState ->
129| currentState.copy(userLocationState = UserLocationState.Success(it))
130| }
131| }
132| }
133|
134| is Resource.Error -> {
135| val errorMessage = getErrorMessage(result.error)
136| updateState { currentState ->
137| currentState.copy(
138| userLocationState = UserLocationState.Error(
139| errorMessage
140| )
141| )
142| }
143| if (manual) emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowError(errorMessage))
144| }
145|
146| is Resource.Loading -> {
147| updateState { currentState ->
148| currentState.copy(userLocationState = UserLocationState.Loading)
149| }
150| }
151| }
152| }
153| }
154| }

159| when (result) {

162| emitSideEffect(
163| SideEffect.ShowSuccess(
164| UiText.StringResource(R.string.location_saved_success)
165| )
166| )
167| }
168|
169| is Resource.Error -> {
170| emitSideEffect(SideEffect.ShowError(getErrorMessage(result.error)))
171| }
172|
173| else -> {
174| }
175| }
176| }
177| }
178| }

404| Snackbar.make(
405| binding.root,

408| ).show()
409| }
410| } else {
411| Snackbar.make(
412| binding.root,
413| getString(R.string.location_required_enable),
414| Snackbar.LENGTH_LONG
415| ).show()
416| }
417| }
418| }

— I saw the runtime crash in your logs:

- Root cause: SecurityException when registering receivers without the new exported flag (Android 14+). 
- Fix I applied: in `BroadcastFragment` I now:
 - Use the new registerReceiver overload on Android 14+ with `Context.RECEIVER_EXPORTED` for the airplane-mode receiver and `Context.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED` for the custom app broadcast.
 - Fall back to the old registerReceiver overload on older Android versions.
 - Call `intent.setPackage(requireContext().packageName)` before sending the custom broadcast so it’s clearly app-local.

Why that fixes the crash
- Android now requires you to explicitly declare whether dynamically-registered receivers are exported or not. The SecurityException in your log is exactly that enforcement. The conditional ensures modern platforms get the required flag while older devices keep compatible behavior.

Notes
- I also made the broadcast-send explicit to the app package to avoid lint warnings and accidental external delivery.
- You’ll still see a lint warning in the editor about the older-API branch (the analyzer detects a path without explicit flags). That’s harmless at runtime (we guard by SDK version) — I can suppress the lint rule if you want the editor quiet.
- Navigation menu warnings in log (NavigationUI: Ignoring onNavDestinationSelected ...) are expected because the bottom nav has items not present in nav_graph; behavior is safe but you may want to align menu item ids with nav destinations.

If you want I can:
- Suppress the lint warning in the broadcast file, or
- Replace bottom-nav IDs with nav_graph destinations (cleaner UX), or
- Run a short runtime smoke test (tap Broadcast, send broadcast, toggle airplane mode) and watch logcat. How broadcast receivers work in this project (short)

- **Where**: receivers live in `presentation/screen/broadcast/BroadcastFragment.kt`. 
- **What two receivers do**:
 - **Airplane Mode receiver** — listens for system airplane-mode changes and updates a TextView. See `airplaneModeReceiver`. 
```27:33:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/broadcast/BroadcastFragment.kt
 private val airplaneModeReceiver = object : BroadcastReceiver() {
 override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) {
 // Keep onReceive fast & simple
 val isOn = intent.getBooleanExtra("state", false)
 statusText.text = if (isOn) "Airplane Mode: ON" else "Airplane Mode: OFF"
 }
 }
```
 - **Custom app broadcast receiver** — listens for an app-specific action `com.example.sababukia_tbc.MY_CUSTOM_BROADCAST` and shows a toast with the `message` extra. See `customReceiver`. 
```36:41:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/broadcast/BroadcastFragment.kt
 private val customReceiver = object : BroadcastReceiver() {
 override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) {
 val message = intent.getStringExtra("message") ?: "No message"
 Toast.makeText(requireContext(), "Received: $message", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
 }
 }
```

## How they’re registered / unregistered
- Receivers are **registered dynamically** in the Fragment’s `onStart()` and **unregistered** in `onStop()` to avoid leaks (and to keep MainActivity clean). 
```70:93:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/broadcast/BroadcastFragment.kt
// registration (uses Android 14+ flags when available; falls back on older APIs)
```
- The code uses the new Android 14 API to explicitly mark receivers as **exported** (system broadcast) or **not exported** (app-internal) and falls back on older overloads for pre-14 devices — this prevents the SecurityException seen on modern Android.

## How the custom broadcast is sent
- The Fragment sends the custom broadcast itself (button click). The Intent is restricted to the app package (via `setPackage(...)`) to avoid accidental external delivery. 
```111:116:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/broadcast/BroadcastFragment.kt
 val intent = Intent(CUSTOM_ACTION)
 intent.putExtra("message", "Hello from custom broadcast!")
 intent.setPackage(requireContext().packageName)
 requireContext().sendBroadcast(intent)
```

## Notes / contrasts
- The app does **not** use BroadcastReceivers for network connectivity; it uses `ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback` instead (more modern, reliable). Example: the `NetworkRepositoryImpl` implements `NetworkCallback` to update a Flow of connectivity state. 
```29:62:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/data/repository/NetworkRepositoryImpl.kt
 private val networkCallback = object : ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback() {
 override fun onAvailable(network: Network) { _isConnected.value = true }
 override fun onLost(network: Network) { /* ... */ }
 override fun onCapabilitiesChanged(network: Network, capabilities: NetworkCapabilities) { /* ... */ }
 }
```

## How to test quickly
- Open app → tap the Broadcast tab (bottom nav) → press **Send Custom Broadcast** (you should see a toast). 
- Toggle airplane mode on the device/emulator — the `statusText` should update to ON/OFF.

Short answer
- **`TAG` is never used** because you declared it but never call it (e.g., in a Log). Either use it when logging or remove it. 
- **`ignored` parameters are never used** because the catch blocks intentionally ignore the exception object. Kotlin flags unused params — either reference the variable (log it), rename to `_` to signal intentional unused, or suppress the warning.

### Quick fixes (pick one)

- Use `TAG` in logs:
```kotlin
// keep TAG
private const val TAG = "BroadcastFragment"
// use it
Log.w(TAG, "unregisterReceiver airplaneModeReceiver failed", ignored)
```

- Mark catch param as intentionally unused (preferred minimal change):
```kotlin
try { requireContext().unregisterReceiver(airplaneModeReceiver) } catch (_: IllegalArgumentException) { }
try { requireContext().unregisterReceiver(customReceiver) } catch (_: IllegalArgumentException) { }
```

- Or log the exceptions instead of ignoring:
```kotlin
catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) {
 Log.w(TAG, "unregisterReceiver failed", e)
}
```

- If you really want to silence lint only:
```kotlin
@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER")
catch (ignored: IllegalArgumentException) { }
```

Recommendation: rename unused catch vars to `_` (cleanest) or log them with `TAG` so both warnings go away and you get useful diagnostics."}]},{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"how did we create a "cluster" of the points in this project"}],"context":[]},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"**Explaining clustering implementation**

- **Dependency (maps + utils)** — we added Google Maps and the Android Maps Utils library so clustering classes are available:

```59:101:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/build.gradle.kts
 // Google Maps and Location
 implementation(libs.google.maps)
 implementation(libs.google.location)
 implementation(libs.google.maps.utils)
```

- **Cluster item** — each location is wrapped in a `ClusterItem` implementation (`LocationClusterItem`) that provides position, title and snippet:

```7:19:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/map/LocationClusterItem.kt
class LocationClusterItem(private val location: LocationUiModel) : ClusterItem {
 override fun getPosition(): LatLng { return location.position }
 override fun getTitle(): String? { return location.name }
 override fun getSnippet(): String? { return location.description }
 // ...
}
```

- **Cluster manager setup** — in `MapFragment.onMapReady()` we create a `ClusterManager<LocationClusterItem>` with the map, set click listeners and a renderer, and wire the map to delegate camera/marker events to the cluster manager:

```208:233:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/map/MapFragment.kt
clusterManager = ClusterManager<LocationClusterItem>(ctx, googleMap)

clusterManager?.setOnClusterClickListener { cluster ->
 val builder = CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom(cluster.position, (googleMap?.cameraPosition?.zoom ?: 0f) + 2f)
 googleMap?.animateCamera(builder)
 true
}

clusterManager?.setOnClusterItemClickListener { item ->
 val location = item.getLocation()
 val bottomSheet = LocationDetailsBottomSheet.newInstance(location)
 bottomSheet.show(childFragmentManager, "LocationDetails")
 true
}

clusterManager?.renderer = object : DefaultClusterRenderer<LocationClusterItem>(ctx, googleMap, clusterManager) { }

googleMap?.setOnCameraIdleListener(clusterManager)
googleMap?.setOnMarkerClickListener(clusterManager)
googleMap?.setOnInfoWindowClickListener(clusterManager)
```

- **Adding items and clustering** — when locations are available we convert each to `LocationClusterItem`, add to the cluster manager and call `cluster()` to group them:

```298:307:D:/AndroidProjects/SabaBukia_TBC/app/src/main/java/com/example/sababukia_tbc/presentation/screen/map/MapFragment.kt
private fun displayLocations(locations: List<Location>) {
 clusterManager?.clearItems()
 locations.forEach { location ->
 val locationUiModel = location.toLocationUiModel()
 val clusterItem = LocationClusterItem(locationUiModel)
 clusterManager?.addItem(clusterItem)
 }
 clusterManager?.cluster()
}
```

How it behaves at runtime
- The maps-utils `ClusterManager` automatically clusters nearby `ClusterItem`s and renders cluster markers via the `DefaultClusterRenderer`. 
- Moving/zooming the map triggers `onCameraIdle` → cluster manager recomputes clusters. 
- Clicking a cluster zooms in (we handle that in `setOnClusterClickListener`). 
- Clicking an individual item shows details (handled in `setOnClusterItemClickListener`).

If you want, I can:
- Customize marker/cluster appearance by overriding `DefaultClusterRenderer.onBeforeClusterRendered` / `onBeforeClusterItemRendered`, or 
- Add a sample that toggles clustering parameters (grid size, min cluster size). // Place inside `MapFragment` (uses existing `googleMap`, `clusterManager`, `LocationClusterItem`)

private fun setupClusterManager() {
 val map = googleMap ?: return

 // create cluster manager
 clusterManager = ClusterManager<LocationClusterItem>(requireContext(), map)

 // optional: custom renderer (or DefaultClusterRenderer)
 clusterManager?.renderer = CustomClusterRenderer(requireContext(), map, clusterManager!!)

 // wrapper camera idle listener that first lets cluster manager do its work,
 // then runs your custom camera-idle logic.
 val cameraIdleListener = GoogleMap.OnCameraIdleListener {
 // Let cluster manager update clusters & markers
 clusterManager?.onCameraIdle()
 // Then run app-specific camera idle logic
 onCameraIdle()
 }

 // wrapper marker click listener that tries your custom handler first,
 // and falls back to cluster manager if not handled.
 val markerClickListener = GoogleMap.OnMarkerClickListener { marker ->
 val handledByApp = handleCustomMarkerClick(marker)
 if (!handledByApp) {
 // delegate to cluster manager (returns true if handled)
 clusterManager?.onMarkerClick(marker) ?: false
 } else {
 true
 }
 }

 // wrapper info window click listener
 val infoWindowClickListener = GoogleMap.OnInfoWindowClickListener { marker ->
 // your custom logic
 handleInfoWindowClick(marker)
 // also notify cluster manager so it can maintain internal state
 clusterManager?.onInfoWindowClick(marker)
 }

 // set the wrapper listeners on the GoogleMap
 map.setOnCameraIdleListener(cameraIdleListener)
 map.setOnMarkerClickListener(markerClickListener)
 map.setOnInfoWindowClickListener(infoWindowClickListener)

 // cluster manager's own cluster/item listeners
 clusterManager?.setOnClusterClickListener { cluster ->
 zoomToCluster(cluster)
 true
 }

 clusterManager?.setOnClusterItemClickListener { item ->
 showLocationDetails(item)
 true
 }

 // Make sure cluster manager also receives map events it expects
 // (we already call clusterManager.onCameraIdle() / .onMarkerClick(...) above)
}
 
private fun onCameraIdle() {
 // custom camera idle behavior (e.g., update UI, request data)
}

private fun handleInfoWindowClick(marker: Marker) {
 // custom info window click behavior
}

private fun handleCustomMarkerClick(marker: Marker): Boolean {
 // return true if handled; false to let cluster manager handle it
 return false
}

private fun zoomToCluster(cluster: Cluster<LocationClusterItem>) {
 val builder = LatLngBounds.Builder()
 for (item in cluster.items) builder.include(item.position)
 googleMap?.animateCamera(CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngBounds(builder.build(), 100))
}
```

Notes:
- This pattern delegates to the cluster manager first (so the utility library can do its cluster/marker work) and then runs app-specific logic — or vice versa as needed.

import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.view.View
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.view.WindowManager
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.TextView
import androidx.fragment.app.DialogFragment
import com.example.mtgcollectionmanager.R
import com.google.android.material.textfield.TextInputEditText

class EditCollectionDialog(
 private val collectionId: Long,
 private val currentName: String,
 private val currentDescription: String,
 private val onUpdateCollection: (collectionId: Long, name: String, description: String) -> Unit
) : DialogFragment() {

 private lateinit var tvDialogTitle: TextView
 private lateinit var etCollectionName: TextInputEditText
 private lateinit var etCollectionDescription: TextInputEditText
 private lateinit var btnCreate: Button
 private lateinit var btnCancel: Button

 override fun onCreateView(
 inflater: LayoutInflater,
 container: ViewGroup?,
 savedInstanceState: Bundle?
 ): View? {
 return inflater.inflate(R.layout.dialog_create_collection, container, false)
 }

 override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
 super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)

 tvDialogTitle = view.findViewById(R.id.tvDialogTitle)
 etCollectionName = view.findViewById(R.id.etCollectionName)
 etCollectionDescription = view.findViewById(R.id.etCollectionDescription)
 btnCreate = view.findViewById(R.id.btnCreate)
 btnCancel = view.findViewById(R.id.btnCancel)

 // Set title and button text for edit mode
 tvDialogTitle.text = "Edit Collection"
 btnCreate.text = "Update"

 // Pre-fill with current values
 etCollectionName.setText(currentName)
 etCollectionDescription.setText(currentDescription)

 btnCreate.setOnClickListener {
 val name = etCollectionName.text?.toString()?.trim() ?: ""
 val description = etCollectionDescription.text?.toString()?.trim() ?: ""

 if (name.isEmpty()) {
 etCollectionName.error = "Collection name is required"
 return@setOnClickListener
 }

 onUpdateCollection(collectionId, name, description)
 dismiss()
 }

 btnCancel.setOnClickListener {
 dismiss()
 }

 // Show keyboard automatically
 etCollectionName.requestFocus()
 etCollectionName.setSelection(etCollectionName.text?.length ?: 0)
 dialog?.window?.setSoftInputMode(WindowManager.LayoutParams.SOFT_INPUT_STATE_VISIBLE)
 }

 override fun onStart() {
 super.onStart()
 dialog?.window?.setLayout(
 ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
 ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT
 )
 }
}
